## ✨ Highlights

- 🎛️ **Tune the kernel for HAProxy, safely**: a node's new **System › Sysctl** page - and `janusctl system sysctl` - changes the kernel parameters HAProxy depends on (accept queues, source ports, TIME_WAIT reuse, SYN-ACK retries, binding to a virtual IP, socket buffers, open files, conntrack...): each within its bounds, **tested on trial** first - the node puts the previous values back by itself unless you apply them -, back to Janus's defaults any time, every change in the node's history. See [Kernel tuning](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/guide/kernel-tuning.md).
- 🛡️ **The CIS benchmark, enforced and locked**: the node's kernel parameters now comply with all 33 kernel-parameter controls of the **CIS Debian Linux 13 Benchmark v1.0.0, Level 2 - Server** - 8 of them didn't - on every network interface too, written at every boot and never changeable, by any call.
- ⚠️ **IPv6 is static from now on**: a node accepts no router advertisement (CIS 3.3.2.7) - no SLAAC address, no route from a router. See the upgrade notes.

## 🎛️ Kernel tuning

- **17 parameters you can change**, no other: `net.core.somaxconn`, `net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range` and `ip_local_reserved_ports`, `tcp_tw_reuse`, `tcp_fin_timeout`, `tcp_synack_retries`, `ip_nonlocal_bind` (IPv4 and IPv6), `net.core.netdev_max_backlog`, `tcp_rmem`/`tcp_wmem`, `fs.file-max`, the three TCP keepalive ones, `tcp_fastopen` and `net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max`. The page shows for each its value, Janus's default, its bounds, what it does to HAProxy, its risks and its sources; values are checked as you type, and again by the node - which also refuses a source port range over a port it listens on, a file limit or a conntrack table below what's in use.
- **Janus's defaults are HAProxy's recommendations**: `somaxconn` 60000, `tcp_tw_reuse` 1, `tcp_fin_timeout` 30, `tcp_synack_retries` 3, `ip_nonlocal_bind` 1, `netdev_max_backlog` 10000; the source port range is 10240-65023, above Janus's own listeners; the parameters that depend on the machine's memory keep the kernel's value.
- **On trial, then applied**: a test lasts 10 minutes by default (1 minute to 1 hour) and counts down on the page; **Apply** keeps the values - saved on the node, set again at every boot -, **Cancel now** puts the previous ones back. HAProxy reloads, without dropping a connection, for the parameters it reads when it opens its listeners.
- **Read-only, with the reason**: `tcp_max_syn_backlog` (no effect with SYN cookies always on - `somaxconn` bounds the SYN queue), `fs.nr_open`, the TCP congestion control; `kernel.core_pattern` is never changed.
- **The history**: who changed what, when, each value before and after - on the node, whoever asked (the Controller, janusctl, your own tools).
- **janusctl**: `janusctl system sysctl list | get | set NAME=VALUE... | reset NAME... / -all | confirm | cancel | history` ([reference](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/guide/janusctl-reference.md#janusctl-system-sysctl)).

## 🛡️ Hardening

- **The benchmark's 8 missing controls**: IPv4 `secure_redirects` and `log_martians`, IPv6 `accept_redirects` and `accept_ra` - each on `all` and `default`. IPv6 never copies those onto the interfaces that already exist, and the first one comes up before Janus's init: until now, it accepted IPv6 redirects and router advertisements whatever the defaults said. The node now writes them on every interface, and checks them there.
- **Locked three times over**: the API only takes the 17 parameters; every boot applies the saved values line by line against the same rules - a line edited on the disk by hand is refused and recorded -, then writes the benchmark's values again and logs the audit (`33/33 controls compliant`); SELinux only lets janusd write the 17 parameters' files.

## 🔌 The node API

- `SystemService`: `SysctlList`, `SysctlApply` (on trial, or `validate_only`), `SysctlConfirm` (over a connection opened after the apply), `SysctlCancel`, `SysctlHistory` - readers list and read the history, admins change ([API reference](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/private-cloud/api-reference.md)). Nothing else changed.

## ⚠️ Upgrade notes

- **Controller first**, as usual: the **Sysctl** page comes with it - and needs nodes on this release (an older node answers that it doesn't know the calls).
- **IPv6 by router advertisement stops**: a node that took its IPv6 address or its IPv6 default route from a router (SLAAC) loses them at the reboot that ends its update. Give it static IPv6 `addresses` and a `gateway6` in its [network configuration](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/network-configuration.md) before updating it. Nodes on IPv4 only, or with static IPv6, aren't concerned.
- **New kernel defaults at that same reboot**: HAProxy's recommended values above. Two to look at:
  - the source port range becomes 10240-65023: if one of your frontends listens above 10240, reserve its port (`net.ipv4.ip_local_reserved_ports`) - the page warns about such a port;
  - `ip_nonlocal_bind` is on: HAProxy can bind a virtual IP on every node of a VRRP pair, but a mistyped `bind` address no longer stops it from starting.

  Any of them goes back to the kernel's value - or another - from the page, on trial.
